description.narrative:
Projektet syftar till att svara på utvecklingsutmaningar relaterat till skadedjur och sjukdomar som är av betydelse inom ramen för allomfattande hälsa i Etiopien och Kenya, och kommer att dra nytta av befintlig expertis inom icipe och existerande partnerskap i länderna. Detta för att bidra till mer resilienta livsmedelssystem, resilient folkhälsa och resilienta socioekonomiska system.
Projektet förväntas bidra till synergier mellan aktörer, samt underlätta spridning av information och innovationer. Projektet "Accelerate One Health" syftar till att adressera diverse utvecklingsutmaningar som påverkar hälsan hos människor, djur, växter och olika ekosystem i Etiopien och Kenya inom ramen för hållbara livsmedelssystem och allomfattande hälsa.
Projektet syftar till att svara på utvecklingsutmaningar relaterat till skadedjur och sjukdomar som är av betydelse inom ramen för allomfattande hälsa i Etiopien och Kenya.
The project aims to respond to development challenges related to pests and diseases of importance in the context of One Health in Ethiopia and Kenya.

description.narrative:
Some examples of results are: 1. A project inception meeting was organised which brought together 25 experts (18 male, 7 female) from the fields of Entomology, Ecology, Pathology, Medicine, Biochemistry, Data science, GIS and modelling, Communication, Socioeconomics and Impact assessment, Gender and Equality, Project Management, Capacity building, Finance and Administration. These experts represented 8 institutions from Kenya and Ethiopia.
2. Through the implementation of ACCLERATEONE HEALTH, icipe has the for the first time being able to convene a meeting that brings on board stakeholders that cut across the 4Hs including the following organization Kenya Plant health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) Zoonotic Disease Unit (ZDU) of the Ministry of Health (MOH), Kenya Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) Technical University of Kenya (TUK) Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) Arbaminch Plant health Clinic (APHC), Ethiopia Ethiopia Public Health Institute (EPHI) Bio and Emerging Technology Institute (BETin), Ethiopia.
3. An online query for Parthenium in Kenya via the GBIF species diversity data portal, revealed its presence the western and central parts of the country in 21 counties. However, these observations were mostly based on roadside surveys. Surveys were initiated to characterise infestation at farm levels. In Homabay, these surveys revealed high infestation densities at spots closer to major roads and the shores of Lake Victoria. Such density maps, will be useful in guiding the deployment of One Health solutions to Parthenium management such as the release of natural enemies and application of bioherbicides.
4. An online datamining exercise was conducted to establish the presence or absence of a One Health strategy or framework draft across the mainland and island nations in Africa. Only 15 (27%) countries in Africa have a framework for OH strategy/frame work draft, with the East African region taking the lead. With regards to One Health peer reviewed publications and policy that focused on Animal and Human Health, South Africa and Madagascar recorded the highest number of publications and policy documents. These disproportionate maps will guide One Health stakeholders on where to channel their efforts towards greater implementation and impact.
